cells.gaps: No count of local offices that enter events in INRIS themselves is published, and the figures disagree: the Minister's 2026 statement has INRIS deployed in eleven districts with no total (ZMB-006), a 2025 case study has access in 81 of 116 districts (ZMB-020), and earlier accounts give 26 district offices and over 40 districts; each is deployment or access, not offices registering. The facts also disagree on where entry is made: ZMB-015 and ZMB-017 have paper forms keyed at provincial or national headquarters, while ZMB-002 has one district office registering through INRIS in September 2026, which does not carry the country. Deaths are reported registered in INRIS (ZMB-010, ZMB-016), though the Minister names death certificates only as intended (ZMB-007). The cost of the exercise is stated without a source of funds (ZMB-009), an older fact naming donors (ZMB-022). Nothing dated inside the twelve months says the system advanced or regressed nationally. ZMB-004 and ZMB-005 are from an excluded source.
cells.note: INRIS is past its pilot and registers births in the districts where it is deployed, with the record keyed at a higher level from the office's paper as routine, which meets stage 3. Stage 4 needs entry at the office held in the national register and more than half of offices registering; the made value is keyed-elsewhere and the newest count is eleven districts with no total.
